chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who migrated and left his wife among the polytheists, then she joined him afterwards: should he retain her in marriage or does her bond of marriage cease? He said, 'No, but he retains her and she is his wife.' And whenever the wife converts to Islam and her husband does not convert, he has the right to the contract of her marriage, except that he does not have sexual relations with her nor is he allowed to be secluded with her.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a Muslim man's marriage to a non-Muslim woman who remains a polytheist after he migrates?
ai.summary: In the context of early Islamic migrations, this hadith clarifies that a woman's conversion does not automatically dissolve the marriage if her husband remains a polytheist, distinguishing between the validity of the contract (‘aqd) and the permissibility of intimacy. Shaykh al-Tusi highlights that while the husband retains the right to the marriage, he is barred from sexual relations or seclusion (khalwah) with her until his own conversion, ensuring stability during the transitional period of religious change. This ruling reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the marriage bond persists even if one spouse is non-Muslim, provided the other is Muslim, contrasting with some Sunni schools that may consider it automatically dissolved.
